newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by reduced packer demand and projections for a slight increase in hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Top prices on interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to packing plants could range from $51.00 to $51.50 and Illinois top prices at plants could span $50.00 to $50.50.
Indiana and Ohio top prices for hogs at plants were seen at $50.00 to $50.50, sources there said.
Pressure also was seen amid IBP's plans to cut the second shift at its Columbus Junction Iowa hog plant on Monday.

The slaughter reduction was announced last Monday and will last indefinitely, IBP officials said. The cut was announced in tandem with news IBP planned to cease hog slaughter at its Council Bluffs, Iowa hog plant effective April 24.
IBP cited industry overcapacity and dwindling local hog supplies for the planned reductions in pork production.
Illinois hog prices could be pressured if workers at Hormel's Rochelle plant strike, livestock dealers said.
Union officials and management at the plant were meeting Friday on a new labor contract, a Hormel spokesman said. He said the company did not anticipate a strike or work stoppage.
